criteria.rationale: I examined the Linux CLI shim enablement in cmd/pose/main.go, the shim child scan and pidfd checks, and the design assessment's empty delta list. Linux dispatch uses its isolated shim; the non-shim embedder fallback remains reviewer-settable under L6; L1-L4 are explicit residuals. Windows has no process-group implementation, which I recorded as N1 rather than treating the L2 assumption as verified.
Linux process ownership and release serialization passed focused unit and race checks, but Windows has no child termination path and can continue cleanup with a live reviewer child.

The change adds the --confirm-abandoned cancel flag and status output while preserving schema-1 run/receipt records. The new cancel CLI branch is a known gap in the spec; I inspected the branch and the store-level release tests, while existing CLI integration evidence covers the delegation surface.

The release refuses live owners, unreadable markers, incomplete run history, and unconfirmed markerless reservations with bounded errors; the full sealed unit evidence and focused release tests cover these paths.
The changed boundary is the pose-mcp CLI/domain ledger; no HTTP, protobuf, Kafka, or MCP tool contract changed. The integration assessment's three unobserved HTTP routes are unrelated to this scope.
The failed cleanup path can label a signalled but unreaped PID as ended. N3 also makes the bounded report's headline count inaccurate above 1,001 processes.
The CLI change is additive, existing record schemas remain unchanged, and the localized command help documents the new confirmation flag.
Linux dispatch reaps the shim subtree before inventory, but Windows builds no-op the process-group functions and can finish inventory with a reviewer child still alive.

D1 addresses the cause of escaped reviewer commands by placing subreaper authority in a single run shim, avoiding dispatcher-wide adoption; D2 closes abandoned attempts through a failed run and receipt. Process-group-only and environment-only cleanup are insufficient for Linux reviewers that setsid or clear their environment. The structural assessment reported no delta facts requiring mapping.
The new fallback comment and manuals claim process-group termination on other platforms, while Windows implements neither process groups nor a kill operation.
The cancel recovery path provides the cause and release command, but an incomplete shim reaping can leave a contradictory ended-PID statement in the failed run record.
R1's process cleanup is not provided on Windows; N2 also falls short of R2's accurate list of terminated processes in the unreaped-child failure case.
The subject changes implement R1-R6, D1-D2 and the paired documentation/template updates; the Linux shim, platform fallback and attempt-release additions stay within the approved pose-mcp surface.

On Linux the shim scan cannot signal the dispatcher or sibling runs, and the fd-3 report closes on exec. On Windows a surviving reviewer child can retain any explicitly authorized environment credential after the run.

The per-run shim is the smallest boundary that handles setsid/environment-clearing descendants without process-wide subreaper effects; pidfds prevent PID-reuse signalling. It adds no cgroup or service-manager controls, so L1 remains the invalidating condition. The Windows fallback mismatch is separately recorded as N1.

findings.action: The non-Linux fallback and manuals claim process-group termination, but the Windows build's isolateProcessGroup and killProcessGroup are no-ops (review_dispatch_windows.go:14-16). A reviewer child can survive while dispatch proceeds to worktree checks and cleanup, so R1 is not met on Windows. Qualify Windows as unsupported and fail closed, or implement safe process-tree termination.
Distinguish signalled PIDs from PIDs verified reaped, and record per-PID residual state on timeout.
findings.rationale: The shim records a PID as ended after SIGKILL delivery but before confirming it was reaped. If the child remains through the reaping deadline, the failed run still says it ended while reporting only a generic residual count.

findings.action: Use EndedTotal for the bounded shim report's headline count and cover a report above 1,001 PIDs.
findings.rationale: When the shim reports more than 1,001 PIDs, the dispatch reports len(reaped), which counts the 1,000 listed PIDs plus one summary placeholder instead of the actual EndedTotal.
